summary: Victor A. van Bijlert is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter. He held posts at IIM Calcutta, Leiden University, and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, retiring in 2021.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale University and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. Around 2004, he became Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia, and he founded the Dalai Lama Center in 2005.
Victor Cousin was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Charlemagne and the Pensionnat normal. He held a post at the University of Paris from around 1815 to 1852.

Victor D'Avella is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2017–2018), the University of Oxford (attested 2021), and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University by 2004 and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).

Victor Goloubew was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Saint Petersburg University and earned a PhD from Heidelberg University. He taught Indian art at INALCO and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and EFEO (1920–1943).

Victor H. Mair was a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD under Patrick Hanan), he taught at Harvard before joining the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1979.

Victor Hehn was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Tartu (ca. 1830–1834). He held posts at the University of Tartu (~1846–1851) and the National Library of Russia (1855–1873).

Victor Henry was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Strasbourg, Burgundy, and Paris under Abel Bergaigne. He held posts at Lille, the University of Douai, and the University of Paris, becoming professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar in 1888.

Victor Herbert Jackson was an Indologist and historian. He joined the Indian Education Service in 1900, taught at Presidency University (~1900–1907), and served as principal of Patna College (~1914–1927).

Victor Michels was a linguist who studied under Paul Deussen, Hermann Osthoff, Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Ernst Windisch, earning a PhD from Leipzig. He held posts at Göttingen (1892) and Jena (1895).

Victor Turner was an anthropologist and scholar of religion who studied at UCL and Manchester (PhD). He worked at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute and taught at Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.
Victoria Lysenko is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Shrinarayan Mishra. She served as Head at the Russian Academy of Sciences and held a post at its Institute of Philosophy.

Victoria Vertogradova is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. She is a chief research fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who earned her PhD from Cambridge. She held posts at Sydney, Hong Kong, SPA Delhi, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University, where she became Barbara Stoler Miller Professor in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Allahabad, Gorakhpur, and under Paul Thieme. He was Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).
Vijay Singh is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD (1998–2002) at Panjab University, where he also served as Professor and Chairperson from 1994.
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri (attested 1933) and founded the Prakrit Text Society.
